sources.title: South Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), on behalf of the Humanitarian Country Team and partners
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 humanitarian conditions and flood/drought observations; 2026 response and logistics planning.
sources.methodology: OCHA consolidated a multi-agency needs assessment and response plan for the Humanitarian Country Team.
sources.limitations: Operational planning synthesis, not a causal evaluation; many figures are regional or national aggregates.

sources.title: Special Report: 2025 FAO/WFP Crop and Food Security Assessment Mission (CFSAM) to the Republic of South Sudan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and World Food Programme
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 crop season and food-security conditions; IPC outlooks through April-July 2026.
sources.methodology: Mission: 20 crop missions in 44 counties, with about 2,500 farmer interviews and 34 focus groups.
sources.limitations: In insecure areas, phone and committee reports substituted for field visits; food-security estimates combine multiple drivers.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief: South Sudan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Information and Early Warning System on Food and Agriculture
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 7 September 2026; 2026 crop performance and food-security conditions.
sources.methodology: GIEWS brief synthesizes cereal balances, earth observation, food prices and IPC analysis.
sources.limitations: Rolling dated snapshot; rainfall forecasts and food-security estimates can change as weather, security and markets evolve.

claims.locator: PDF p. 6, Part 1, section 1.1, Climate Variability.
claims.paraphrase: By November 2025, floods in Greater Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei had affected over 1.3 million people and displaced over 375,000, while northern and south-eastern regions faced prolonged dry spells; women and girls faced increased workloads and GBV exposure.
claims.limitations: HNRP operational figures; no local climate attribution is estimated.

claims.locator: PDF p. 7, Part 1, section 1.1, Conflict and Climate stress further acts as a conflict multiplier.
claims.paraphrase: The plan says flood displacement pushed pastoralists into farming zones, reigniting farmer-herder clashes; drought-stricken regions faced renewed competition over water points and grazing land.
claims.limitations: This humanitarian planning synthesis does not estimate causal effects or local prevalence of clashes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: OCHA explicitly links flood displacement and drought-related resource pressure with renewed farmer-herder clashes and competition.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 7, Part 1, section 1.1, Climate stress further acts as a conflict multiplier.

claims.locator: PDF p. 29, Part 3, section 3.6, Logistics, Summary of needs.
claims.paraphrase: Erratic rainfall and flooding damaged humanitarian supply routes and prevented pre-positioning; violence and insecurity also disrupted commercial movements and aid access.
claims.limitations: Operational account of humanitarian access, not a measure of adaptation-project reach.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: HNRP says climate-related flooding and violence each disrupt routes, logistics and timely humanitarian access.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 29, Part 3, section 3.6, Logistics, Summary of needs.

claims.paraphrase: Jonglei, Lakes and Unity held 88% of flood-affected people; flooding was less extensive in western Sudd, Tonj (Warrap) and Greater Bahr el Ghazal than in earlier years.
claims.limitations: Flooding varied regionally, not uniformly by state.

claims.locator: PDF p. 28, section Flooding and crop performance.
claims.paraphrase: Farmers in flood-prone areas planted more on higher ground; late flooding limited damage as crops were mature.
claims.limitations: Planting shifts, flood timing and crop maturity effects are not separated.

claims.locator: PDF p. 53, section Drivers of household food insecurity.
claims.paraphrase: Food insecurity reflected conflict, low production, economic shocks and depleted coping; 2025 floods added multi-sector needs amid reduced funding and insecurity-related access constraints.
claims.limitations: Multiple drivers are identified; causal shares are not assigned.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: CFSAM reports flood-affected needs alongside access constraints stemming from heightened insecurity in 2025.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 53, section Drivers of household food insecurity.

claims.locator: PDF p. 13, section Crop and food security assessment mission methodology.
claims.paraphrase: Where insecurity barred field visits, CFSAM used phone interviews and crop-monitoring committee data.
claims.limitations: Substitute reports are not direct observations.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: CFSAM says high insecurity prevented field visits in some areas.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 13, section Crop and food security assessment mission methodology.

claims.locator: GIEWS section Concerns for 2026 cereal production due to dry weather conditions, first paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: In southern agricultural areas, prolonged dry spells harmed 2026 first-season maize and sorghum development, and FAO estimated below-average output.
claims.limitations: Country-brief synthesis; it gives no subregional yield estimates.

claims.locator: GIEWS section Concerns for 2026 cereal production due to dry weather conditions, forecast paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: The 7 September brief forecast that rainfall deficits could constrain central and northern yields, while above-average October-December rains could support southern second-season crops.
claims.scenario: FAO's 2026 near-term weather forecast; no climate-model scenario is specified.
claims.limitations: This is a dated weather forecast, not a verified harvest outcome.

claims.locator: GIEWS section Concerns for 2026 cereal production due to dry weather conditions, closing paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports insecurity intensified from late 2025 and disrupted agricultural activity in some areas, likely contributing to localized crop shortfalls.
claims.scenario: Qualitative FAO assessment based on insecurity; affected locations and crop-loss estimates are unspecified.
claims.limitations: The brief does not identify affected locations or quantify the conflict-related production effect.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO says heightened insecurity disrupted agricultural activities and likely caused localized crop shortfalls.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: GIEWS section Concerns for 2026 cereal production due to dry weather conditions, closing paragraph.

search_audit.query: South Sudan FAO WFP CFSAM 2025 flooded counties 2026 crop production named counties report
search_audit.outcome: Found a full FAO/WFP crop assessment with county-level 2025 flood exposure and farmer responses, plus the HNRP's Greater Upper Nile flood and northern/south-eastern dry-spell account.

search_audit.query: South Sudan climate flood displacement farmer herder conflict water grazing 2026 OCHA humanitarian plan
search_audit.outcome: Found an HNRP statement that flood displacement can renew farmer-herder clashes and drought can intensify competition over water and grazing; it is a planning synthesis, not a causal evaluation.

search_audit.query: South Sudan 2025 insecurity access crop production humanitarian assistance conflict assessment report counties
search_audit.outcome: Found CFSAM evidence that insecurity made some crop-assessment sites too dangerous for teams, requiring phone and community-monitoring substitutes; GIEWS also reports insecurity disrupting agricultural activity.

search_audit.query: South Sudan farmers plant on high ground flood adaptation resilience CFSAM 2025 evaluation communities
search_audit.outcome: Found CFSAM reporting that farmers in flood-prone areas shifted planting from low ground to higher ground; the mission does not isolate this practice's effect from flood timing.

gaps: The HNRP's official OCHA page returned 403; the complete report was read from a third-party PDF mirror, whose cover and about-page identify the source as OCHA-consolidated.
The FAO DOI landing page for CFSAM returned 403; the full report PDF was accessible through the South Sudan CLIMIS portal.
Some CFSAM locations were too insecure for field teams; telephone and community-crop-monitoring reports reduce direct observation in those areas.
The 2026 FAO GIEWS brief is a 7 September snapshot; seasonal forecasts and security/market conditions may have changed by later 2026.

Climate-FCV material is strongest for flood-related displacement and resource competition in the HNRP's broad affected-area framing; it does not quantify local causal effects or establish uniform conflict outcomes.
The DTM August 2025 flood-displacement report was inaccessible; current subnational displacement detail beyond the accessible HNRP and CFSAM remains incomplete.
